scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4659: Hi, the campus network keeps going slow for us in
bursts -- transfers crawl for a bit, then recover, then crawl again. A couple
of the more technical people here keep saying "the main router is dropping
our packets" (they call it router0), but I honestly wouldn't know a packet if
I saw one. All I can tell you is it keeps going slow in waves for everyone.
Could someone check whether something really is losing our traffic and sort
it out? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 has ip_forward enabled, its interfaces
  are up, and traffic transiting router0 between segments arrives with 0% loss; there
  is no drop-inducing ACL or forwarding fault. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of packet loss on router0 that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router0 dropping/forwarding
traffic incorrectly -- is NOT reproducible: a ping across router0 (between two
segments it connects) completes with 0% loss, router0 has ip_forward enabled, its
interfaces are up, ripd is running, and there is no drop-inducing ACL.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router0 is forwarding correctly and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a path transiting
router0, finds 0% loss, checks router0's ip_forward, interfaces, and any filters, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" router0 dropping packets -- blaming an ACL,
forwarding, or load to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report described periodic bursts of slow transfers affecting the whole campus, with finger-pointing at router0 as a packet-dropper. A thorough four-phase diagnostic sweep finds no evidence of any such fault.

**Affected component:** None identified. All candidate fault classes were inspected.

**Mechanism investigated:** The bursty-slowness pattern is consistent with link flapping (brief carrier loss), injected traffic shaping (tc tbf/netem), ACL-based rate-limiting, or a stress/DoS process. Each of these leaves a specific trace.

**Localization findings:** Router0's carrier-change counters read exactly 2 on each of its three interfaces (eth0, eth1, eth2) — the startup-only baseline. TX/RX error and drop counters are zero. The kernel log contains no link-down, carrier-loss, or error events. The tc_snapshot confirmed all 43 lab interfaces carry only the default `fq_codel` scheduler with no token-bucket or netem injection. The infra_sweep across all 30 devices found no ACL rules, no ARP anomalies, no addressing misconfigurations, and no resolver divergence. The pressure_sweep detected no stress tools, CPU spikes, or socket floods on any device. The dhcp_link_history helper found no link-flap or DHCP-recovery history. The Phase 1 reachability snapshot showed 0% loss on all tested paths.

**Root cause:** No anomaly exists in the current lab state; every diagnostic indicator for the reported symptom class is at its clean baseline.

**Fix:** No corrective action required. The reported slowness is unconfirmed by any mechanism or historical trace on the live topology; the fault either did not occur as described or has fully self-resolved without leaving evidence.
